messages:
Ava Park: Heads-up: I'm scheduling a thermal sweep for az-west1 GPU racks next Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC. Plan is rolling node drains + soft reboots (no kernel patch). Expect ~12-18% capacity impact on the 'gradient' pool. Need backfill + customer comms.
Ravi Patel: ETA on how many nodes will be cordoned at once? we should cap to avoid SLA misses.
Sam O'Neill: Planning to cordon cohorts of 5 nodes every 20m, staggered across racks. gradient pool has 120 nodes total, ~40 GPUs reserved for Dedicated. So worst-case throughput drop ~15%.
Claire Gomez: Can we warm KV/prefix caches after each cohort? otherwise latency spikes will look worse than capacity loss. Suggest seeding cache with recent hot prefixes before resuming traffic.
Ava Park: yes - KV seed hook after each drain window. ops playbook will run a post-drain job: `curl -X POST https://infra-api/internal/kv-seed?pool=gradient`
Ravi Patel: cost question — if we temporarily spin up on-demand nodes for backfill, what's the ballpark for 3 hours? Quick calc: 10 gpus * $2.5/hr * 3h = $75. But need to account for preemptible vs reserved.
Sam O'Neill: we can use a mix: 6 preemptible + 4 on-demand. Preemptibles are cheaper but risk reclaim. Ops autoscaler can prefer preemptible, fallback to on-demand if capacity not reached.
Claire Gomez: reminder: update routing policy to fall back to eu-central for high-latency-sensitive routes during the window. That reduces tail latency but increases egress cost.
Ava Park: acknowledged. I'll draft customer comms after we lock the backfill numbers. Can someone confirm eviction grace settings? we should avoid killing long-running customer jobs.
Sam O'Neill: using `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300` for most workloads. For long jobs we have a special annotation `infra/allow-evict=false` to skip.
Ravi Patel: can we add a quick health-probe before and after each cohort? say run `python infra/scripts/latency_probe.py --pool gradient` and abort next cohort if 95p latency doubles.
Ava Park: yes — probe + canary. If probe fails, we pause and notify #oncall. ops-bot will create an incident if we hit the threshold.
ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: thermal-sweep-az-west1 (6155559877). Window Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC. Auto-notify: #customers, #support, #gpucapacity.
Claire Gomez: one more: prefix cache seeding needs a KV snapshot. I'll put a small eval set in `s3://infra-seeds/gradient/last-7d.json` for the seed job.
Sam O'Neill: can someone approve 4x on-demand burst nodes in the cost center? putting notes in the PR. @Finance please review.
Ravi Patel: tagging @Finance-team in support message. Also FYI we'll add a short blurb in Console: "Planned maintenance: brief capacity impact, auto-fallback to eu-central".
Ava Park: thanks team. I'll post the external comms draft in #customer-commms tomorrow and link the runbook. Plan: start with single-cohort canary at 02:00, hold 10m, run probe, then continue if healthy.
Claire Gomez: :thumbsup: and I'll monitor cache hit-rate dashboards in realtime.
Sam O'Neill: I'll run a quick dry-run in staging tonight with the exact drain cadence. Cmd snippet for runbook:
```
# cordon + drain example
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
# post-drain seed
curl -X POST https://infra-api/internal/kv-seed?node=gpu-node-42&pool=gradient
```
Ravi Patel: sounds good. Set ops-bot to ping oncall 10m before canary.
ops-bot: will notify oncall at 01:50 UTC.
Ava Park: I'll follow up with runbook link and customer comms. Closing thread for now — will reopen if any blockers.
